title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets) for automorphisms of the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Concretely, this is the profinite free group on two generators, with loops ε_0, ε_1, ε_∞ whose product is 1 and with l_i = ε_i^2.

The objects. The group M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] consists of (outer) automorphisms u written in the normal form u = u_ξ = u_{ξ,η}. Here ξ (or α) is a twisting element and μ = 2ν+1 is the multiplicator, so that u(ε_1) = int(ξ)(ε_1^μ). The automorphism ρ has order 3 and permutes the three cusps. The key cocycle condition is ξ·ρ(ξ)·ρ²(ξ) = 1. This is Grothendieck's analogue of the 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.

Where the page sits. The previous page singled out τ_∞ as the only nontrivial element that can be written explicitly. τ_∞ is the involution corresponding to the element τ of T_{0,3} ≅ Z/2. Its data are listed in (59): ξ = l_1^{-1}, η = 1, ν = μ = -1. The top line of this page, numbered (60) in the image, completes that list: i = 1, α_3 = 1 (i.e. ε_3 = -1), j' = -1.

The remark. Grothendieck asks: which u_{ξ,η} (not necessarily normalized) satisfy f = 1 and β = 1, i.e. η = 1? He recalls that α = 1 (ξ = 1) already forces u = 1.

1. With η = 1 one gets ξ = η·l_1^ν = l_1^ν. It remains only to impose ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1.
2. Push this into SL(2,Ẑ) via the congruence (Sanov-type) realization of the free group. There l_1 = ε_1^2 maps to the unipotent matrix (1 0; 2 1), so ξ maps to (1 0; 2ν 1).
3. A lemma from an earlier page (p. 394?) classifies the elements X = (A B; C D) of SL(2,Ẑ) with Xρ(X)ρ²(X) = 1. Either X = ±ρ^{-1} = ±(-1 1; 1 0), or C + D - B = ±1.
4. The first alternative is impossible, since B = 0 here.
5. The second gives 2ν + 1 = μ = ±1 in Ẑ, so ν = 0 or ν = -1.
6. These are exactly the two trivial solutions: u_ξ = id and u_ξ = τ_∞.

Conclusion. The SL(2,Ẑ) image gives only a necessary condition, but both candidates are genuine solutions, so the classification is complete. The only elements with η = 1 are 1 and τ_∞.

Role in the argument. This is a rigidity statement used on the next page. There it supports the Proposition that the centralizer of τ in N_{0,3}^{!~} is {1, τ}. That proof also ends in an equation of the form ξ^{-1}τ_∞(ξ) = l_1^{-2ν}.

The oblique marginal note is mostly illegible. It seems to say that one thereby re-checks the facts and sees that it is indeed the commutation (of τ_∞ with u) that is being verified, giving a justification of the coefficients.
errors: No mathematical error detected. The SL(2,Ẑ) reduction gives only a necessary condition, but this is harmless because both surviving values ν = 0, -1 are actual solutions (id and τ_∞).
The transcription's 'η = η l_1^ν = l_1^ν' should read 'ξ = η l_1^ν = l_1^ν'; this is a transcription slip, not Grothendieck's.

ideas.what: Testing the cocycle/triangle relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 for automorphisms of π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) by projecting to SL(2,Ẑ) via the congruence-subgroup embedding of the free group, using a classification lemma for solutions in SL(2,Ẑ)
ideas.modern_name: Abelian/linear (SL2 or metabelian) shadows of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and Drinfeld for the GT relations; Lochak–Schneps and others for computations in quotients

ideas.what: Rigidity: the only automorphisms in M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] with η=1 are the identity and the involution τ_∞; this feeds into the statement that the centralizer of τ is {1,τ}
ideas.modern_name: Triviality of the centralizer of the order-2 element in (a variant of) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group / Out of the profinite free group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in GT theory, e.g. Drinfeld; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps on torsion and centralizers in GT

deep.surprise_reason: A short, correct, routine verification within Grothendieck's private development of a GT-like group. It confirms that only the trivial solutions exist, using an SL(2,Ẑ) shadow. The method and result are standard in spirit, and nothing on the page appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The equation number at the top is (60), not (50); it follows (59) on the previous page and precedes (61) on the next.
'On devra avoir η = η l_1^ν = l_1^ν' should read 'On devra avoir ξ = η l_1^ν = l_1^ν'.
'celui-ci se traduit que' should read roughly 'cela se traduit (en) que' / 'ceci se traduit par': in SL(2,Ẑ)', ξ = (1 0; 2ν 1).
'Ceci signifie (p. 394?) qu'on ait soit ...' — the word 'soit' is present in the image, and the page reference may be 394 or 398.
